A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research question, corpus, experiments and evaluation framework. The main text, figures, tables and Appendices A-E support reliable comparison despite reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM-versus-human scoring and feedback experiments, framework validation, and reliability analyses in Sections 4-6 and Appendices B-D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results and additionally reports assessment-completion counts for existing model configurations in Table 11.

M1.justification: The framework is named ProEval, but its extraction, classification and correction-relevance steps remain unchanged, as do the appendix prompts. The model versions highlighted in v2 Section 4 were already specified in v1 Appendix B.1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same corpus of 141 literature reviews from 51 L2 graduate students, covering five topics and nine assessment criteria. No new dataset, population, task or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain human assessors B, C and F, GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5 and Llama-3. The GPT-4o model-variant comparisons in the reliability experiments are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The three interaction modes, default prompts, decoding conditions, metrics and one-factor-at-a-time reliability design are retained. Exact co-assessment counts and clearer descriptions of correlation averaging document existing experiments rather than establish changed settings.

E4.justification: The specificity/helpfulness analysis, prompting and model-variant reliability tests, correction-relevance error analysis, and comment-pair case studies are retained. The relocated score-comment heatmaps contain the same analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain the existing standard-deviation reporting and two temperature=1 runs in Table 4. No new repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports incomplete assessment outputs in Table 11: Llama-3 assessed 140 essays in IM 1 and 139 in IM 2, while Gemini-1.5 assessed 140 in IM 1. The matched scoring, feedback-quality, framework-validation and reliability results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, assessment criteria and score-agreement definitions remain unchanged. Neither version adds formal theoretical results, proofs or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: Both retain the central claims that LLMs provide reasonably good and generally reliable analytic assessments, alongside the corpus and interpretable feedback-evaluation framework contributions. Naming ProEval and emphasizing its fine-grained evaluation restate existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a tentative training-data-overlap explanation for stronger LLM-LLM scoring agreement and explains why some assessment criteria are more objective. It also expands the rationale for evaluating observable problems instead of direct quality ratings. The existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds exact co-assessment denominators and missing-output information in Table 11, clarifies correlation averaging in Section 6.1, and explicitly states in the abstract that code accompanies the corpus release. The underlying pipeline models and prompt templates were already documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds Doddapaneni et al. (2024) on evaluator blind spots and OpenAI's 2023 GPT-4 technical report. It also identifies the ASAP corpus and school grades in its discussion of Stahl et al. (2024), modestly sharpening the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 introduces ProEval terminology, divides Section 4 into framework and validation subsections, condenses the previous-studies discussion, and moves corpus-preparation details into Section 3. It adds explanatory prose and acknowledgments while retaining most of the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 11, color-codes corresponding problem passages in Table 8, and redraws Figure 2 with LLM icons while preserving its validation values. Figures 5 and 6 and several tables relocate; the other embedded figures retain identical content.

improvement.justification: The new co-assessment counts and disclosure of incomplete LLM outputs make the comparisons easier to audit. Clearer framework organization and the color-coded example improve readability. These resolve limited documentation and presentation gaps; the experimental validation remains unchanged, and the added training-data-overlap explanation remains untested.
